title: Large-scale dynamics of integrable quenches
abstract: The Ballistic Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (BMFT) is a path-integral based approach to treat large-scale correlations in interacting integrable systems which, so far, has only been applied to quasi-equilibrium settings. In this paper we extend this approach to integrable quench problems and, to illustrate it, we compute the time evolution of the full-counting-statistics (FCS) of a conserved charge. We identify the relevant path integral, solve it via saddle-point, and obtain a set of partial differential equations describing the dynamics of the FCS. We solve these equations explicitly for free fermionic systems and for the interacting cellular automaton Rule 54. In both cases, we recover the known exact results. For Rule 54, our construction moreover completes the solution across the entire ballistic window.
summary: This paper extends the Ballistic Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (BMFT) to describe large-scale fluctuations in integrable quantum systems after a quench. By treating the problem via a path integral and solving it using saddle-point methods, the authors derive the time evolution of the Full-Counting-Statistics. They successfully apply this generalized theory to model both free fermions and the Rule 54 cellular automaton.
main_problem: The paper extends the Ballistic Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (BMFT) to analyze large-scale correlations in integrable quantum systems following a quench, moving beyond quasi-equilibrium settings.
main_result: The time evolution of the Full-Counting-Statistics (FCS) is determined by solving saddle-point equations derived from the path integral, yielding exact solutions for free fermions and the Rule 54 cellular automaton.
method: The authors employ a path-integral formulation based on BMFT, solving the resulting partial differential equations (PDEs) via saddle-point approximation to track the evolution of the FCS.
model_or_system: The study focuses on integrable quantum many-body systems, specifically testing the formalism on free fermions and the interacting cellular automaton Rule 54, which are characterized by conserved charges and quasiparticle excitations.
key_observables: Full-Counting-Statistics (FCS) of a conserved charge, rapidity distributions ($ho_{t,	heta}$), pseudo-energy ($\epsilon_	heta$), and free energy density ($f$).
important_parameters: The analysis is performed in the ballistic limit ($T \propto X$) and involves parameters related to the initial state preparation and the system's conserved charges.
main_assumptions: The formalism assumes the existence of a well-defined quasiparticle content and relies on extending the BMFT framework from quasi-equilibrium to the quench regime.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the necessary mathematical machinery using specific models (Free Fermions, Rule 54) to derive the governing PDEs for the FCS, and then solving these equations explicitly for the chosen systems.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalized framework (BMFT) to study non-equilibrium dynamics in integrable quantum systems, which is highly relevant for understanding quench dynamics in quantum simulators or ultracold atomic systems.
